subject: Operational handback & tiered latency attribution proposal
messages:
From: Elaine Chang <elaine@sequencelabs.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: Mike Torres <mike.torres@sequencelabs.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: tiered attribution playbook for our private VPC deployment

Connor — thanks again for taking the call last week. As discussed, Sequence Labs is moving a significant batch of RL inference to Redwood's Private offering but our edge egress and transit (third‑party WAN peering) introduce periodic latency spikes that are outside our control. We need an operational agreement that: 1) keeps our customer SLAs tight for the product team; 2) clearly allocates responsibility for different latency bands; and 3) preserves a path to rollback/mitigate without having to open an emergency support ticket every time we see a 95th percentile blip.

Attached is a first pass (draft_amendment_v1.pdf) where we propose a tiered attribution model:
- Tier A: infra within Redwood control (serving runtime, kernel/quant stacks) — Redwood takes full SLO responsibility.
- Tier B: transit/peering variability between Sequence edge PoPs and Redwood colo — attribution shared by measured telemetry with a handback procedure when external latency > X ms sustained for Y minutes.
- Tier C: customer-managed edge and on‑prem segments — Sequence accepts operational responsibility but asks Redwood to provide instrumentation hooks and runbook steps for graceful degradation (cache warmers, fallback model variant).

High level asks: can Redwood commit to instrumentation endpoints for roundtrip/egress latencies, an automatic fallback to a quantized model variant when upstream latency breaches the agreed threshold, and a signing cadence for the amendment? We can be flexible on thresholds but want a repeatable runbook rather than ad‑hoc escalations.

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Chang
Head of Platform Operations | Sequence Labs
[Attachment: draft_amendment_v1.pdf (PDF)]

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Elaine Chang <elaine@sequencelabs.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: tiered attribution playbook for our private VPC deployment

Elaine — thanks for the clear writeup and the draft. I’ve looped in Karthik (infra) and Kimberly (legal) so we can scope the technical telemetry and the contractual language in parallel. Quick clarifying questions up front:
1) Can you share representative p99/p95 latency samples for the last 30 days (edge → Redwood ingress) so we have an empirical baseline?
2) For Tier B handback, are you proposing absolute thresholds (ms) or relative deltas (compared to baseline)?
3) Are you expecting Redwood to run automatic model‑variant failover, or a recommended playbook for your ops team to trigger?

We can respond with a technical instrumentation proposal by EOD Wednesday and a legal draft by Friday next week. If you’re available Thursday we can do a 30‑minute walkthrough of the proposed runbook + fallback behavior.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: runbook-diff.xlsx (XLSX) — quick diff of our suggested runbook changes]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, Elaine Chang <elaine@sequencelabs.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 5 Sep 2028 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: tiered attribution playbook for our private VPC deployment

Thanks Elaine — useful framing. A few technical proposals from infra:
- Measurement points: we can expose telemetry at three points (in order): client egress RTT reported via a lightweight SDK ping, front‑door ingress latency at the colo NIC, and inference service queuing + model execution time. Combining these yields attribution windows.
- Threshold model: prefer a hybrid approach — absolute thresholds for emergency handback (e.g., external egress > 120ms sustained for 10m) and delta thresholds for operational alerts (e.g., >40ms above 30‑day baseline p95).
- Automated mitigation: we can implement an automated fallback to a lower‑precision quantized variant for a configurable % of traffic when egress latency breaches emergency thresholds; full traffic failover requires explicit ops approval (button/Playbook).
- Evidence: we will publish a signed telemetry sample (30 days) and a deterministic script you can run to reproduce.

Open questions: how do you want to handle billing credits if Tier B attribution flips between sides during a single incident window? We can propose a time‑weighted formula but wanted to flag this for finance/legal.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principle Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Tue, Sep 5, 2028 at 08:45 AM Elaine Chang <elaine@sequencelabs.com> wrote:
> Connor/Karthik — we can provide the 30‑day p95/p99 snapshot and prefer absolute thresholds for the emergency handback. For credits, Sequence prefers a simple rule (e.g., if >50% of latency impact attributable to transit, a partial credit scaled to the impacted tokens). Happy to detail in the draft.
> 
> —Elaine

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Elaine Chang <elaine@sequencelabs.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Sep 2028 10:51:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: tiered attribution playbook for our private VPC deployment

Team — from a contract perspective we should keep the amendment narrowly scoped and operational (runbook + measurement framework + credit formula) and avoid expanding core liability beyond current commitments. Proposed legal points:
- Add a defined term "Attributable Network Transit" with clear measurement points.
- Emergency handback clause: when Attributable Network Transit exceeds Emergency Threshold for >10 minutes, Redwood will trigger the mitigation playbook and inform Sequence within 5 minutes.
- Credit formula: time‑weighted split for the incident window, with a cap at 25% of the impacted invoice line for the billing period unless an independent post‑incident forensic review yields different attribution.
- Audit & reproductions rights: Sequence may request up to two forensic exports per quarter. Redwoods agrees to provide telemetry exports and signed digests for those exports.

I’ll mark these into the draft amendment and circulate a redline. If Seq wants higher credit caps we should handle that in commercial terms (deal addendum) rather than core SLA language.

Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

From: Elaine Chang <elaine@sequencelabs.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 8 Sep 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: tiered attribution playbook for our private VPC deployment

Appreciate the quick turnaround and sensible framing. The emergency thresholds look workable — we’ll generate the 30‑day p95/p99 export and upload to the Drive link you shared. We’re comfortable with the cap at 25% for the first contract year; we’ll raise commercial uplift in renewal discussions if our volume trends justify a higher cap.

Next steps on our side: upload telemetry snapshot by EOD Monday, review Kimberly’s redline when it lands, and schedule the 30‑minute walkthrough Thursday at 10am PT. I’ll also initiate the DocuSign envelope with the current draft so legal can see the redline context.

Thanks — Elaine
Head of Platform Operations | Sequence Labs
